subject: Information Theory
title: Shannon's Channel Capacity
description: A short lesson to help you apply Shannon's Channel Capacity.

hook.text: There's a speed limit for data. No matter how clever your code, you can never exceed the channel capacity.

buildup.text: Shannon's formula: C = B log₂(1 + SNR). Capacity depends only on bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio.

discovery.text: Double the bandwidth, double the capacity. Double the SNR and capacity grows—but logarithmically, not linearly.

twist.text: Shannon proved you can transmit at any rate below C with near-zero errors. Above C, errors are unavoidable.

climax.text: Modern systems like 5G operate within 1-2 dB of Shannon's limit. We've nearly maxed out the physics.

punchline.text: Bandwidth times log of SNR. Nature's speed limit.

quiz.question: What determines channel capacity according to Shannon?
